name: 1815 Prairie Avenue — Joseph Sears house (Arthur Meeker's from 1893)

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B stone dwelling (D)'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1841 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

research_note: Refined from the district draft (T-2330) in place by T-3155 (piece 1 of T-1893), under the draft's own id, as a K01 stone-fronted house read off the two photographs Chicagology reproduces (chicagology_1815_sears_two_views: a square-on view and an oblique from the south-west, undated) against the 1911 sheet's plan: the front with its north pavilion under a steep hipped roof, the door under a bracketed hood up its stoop, the corner bay with its pierced stone balcony, the mansard with its gabled dormer, the stair projection and the canted bay on the flanks, and the rear range. T-3562 (the owner's ruling, 2026-11-21): the Chicagology prints show Joseph Sears's front before Arthur Heun's 1902 remodel for the Meekers; the 1904 ground floor is rebuilt to the Chicago Daily News picture of 1908 (cdn_dn0005529_meeker_residence_1908, DN-0005529), its third reference view: the one-storey stone bay across the front, the arched entrance at grade in a block north of the front, and the tall iron railing on the street line. The three views' cameras and match records are in data/reference_views/sears_meeker_house_1815_prairie/.

documented_range.note: The 1904 target to the 1911 sheet that draws the house: the T-1841 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). The photographs are undated; their dating is in the match record.

position.symbolic_location: 1815 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1815 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 18th to 20th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 28).
position.note: The front block's rear north corner: lot frame u 17.5, v -7.12 (the draft's frame point u 7.25, v -1.12 through its own rotation), where the 1911 sheet's trace (s28fp-1815-b1) runs the north wall behind the stair projection (v -7.07 to -7.17) and the front's main plane at u 34.96. The draft's fit of the sheet stands behind it (its georeference's independent check 1.47 m RMS). Rotation 179.45 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The front block read off the 1911 sheet's trace (s28fp-1815-b1 p1) in the lot frame: the front's main plane at u 34.96, the north wall at v -7.12 and the south wall at v 3.35, 10.47 m along the front; 17.46 m deep to lot u 17.5, so the sheet's canted south-flank bay (u 18.1-25.6) stands on it. The stair projection on the north flank, the canted flank bay and the rear range (to u 9.6) stand on it as K08 bays and a K01 rear wing (the corner bay the prints draw went in the 1902 remodel, T-3562; the 1908 Daily News picture draws the one-storey bay and the entrance block before the front instead). T-3562: built 9.72 m along the front, not the sheet's 10.47. Both photographs stand the corner bay's south face about 0.75 m south of the main front's south wall (the oblique: the cornice turns onto the flank at about x 1605-1655 px and the bay's south face shows at x 1745-1790 px; the square-on: the upper wall's south edge at x 834 px and the bay's at x 905 px), and the bay keeps its place on the front, its canted junction (6.99 m) close against the window column at 6.1 m; so the main south wall stands 0.75 m inside the bay's south face, at 9.72 m. The 1911 sheet is the remodelled house (no corner bay); its south wall on the line of the bay's south face is read as the remodel's, which a 1904 front built to the photographs does not take (L-k01-1815-sears-1893).

stories.note: Two wall storeys over a raised basement under a mansard, read off the square-on photograph (the left of the two views, Chicagology; 71.5 px/m on the front's plane, grade at y 1040 px): the 1911 sheet's '3B' counts the mansard storey.

construction.note: The 1911 sheet colours the whole house blue, 'stone'; the photograph shows a smooth light ashlar street front (the 1973 landmarks report: 'yellow limestone'). K01 lays stone on the street front only, so the flanks and rear stand in brick: the photograph's rock-faced south flank is open in the match record.

principal_floor_m.note: The door's threshold at y 915 px on the square-on photograph (the left of the two views, Chicagology; 71.5 px/m on the front's plane, grade at y 1040 px).

In the 1908 Daily News picture (DN-0005529, the owner's 640 x 461 px copy; camera daily_news_dn0005529.json, 3.3 px rms) the arched door stands at grade in the entrance block north of the front (its foot at y 363 px, behind the street railing), not up the old stoop to the principal floor; built one riser over grade, 0.15 m (K01's least for a door carried by a set-out block is 0.12 m, a T-3562 option), the step itself reconstructed.

roof_covering.note: Slate on the mansard's faces and the pavilion's roof, laid in plain courses, on the square-on photograph (the left of the two views, Chicagology; 71.5 px/m on the front's plane, grade at y 1040 px) and the oblique; the deck above the sight line in painted standing-seam tin, and the flashing, are reconstructed.

window_kit.note: K06's two-over-two sash for the flat-headed lights; the photograph's principal-storey windows have leaded upper lights the kit does not carry, open in the match record.

stone_front.note: Smooth coursed ashlar in light stone across the whole street front on the square-on photograph (the left of the two views, Chicagology; 71.5 px/m on the front's plane, grade at y 1040 px), its basement storey laid in two broad courses under a plinth course at the principal floor (K02's channelled base, its channels 18 mm: a finer joint than the print can show, within tolerance). The fabric is K02's Lemont limestone for the 1973 landmarks report's 'yellow limestone' (a secondary reading); its exact quarry is reconstructed. T-3562: the south flank (K01's north wall) is the same stone, rock-faced: on the oblique photograph (the right of the two views, x 1605-1790 px) it reads dark and broken against the smooth front, its faces catching the light stone by stone, where the build laid it in buff common brick. It is laid on the front's beds in the profile's rock face (stone_front.flanks); the print lays it as broken-coursed random ashlar, the build as even courses on the front's lines, a joint pattern under a visitor's notice. That the flank is the front's Lemont stone and not another is inferred from the one reading of the fabric.

street_front_trim.note: Flat-headed openings in both storeys on the square-on photograph (the left of the two views, Chicagology; 71.5 px/m on the front's plane, grade at y 1040 px).

wall_head.note: A deep stone cornice on blocks over a dentil course at the second storey's head, y 357-430 px on the square-on photograph (the left of the two views, Chicagology; 71.5 px/m on the front's plane, grade at y 1040 px). T-3561: enlarged, the square-on print draws under the corona a close row of carved stone consoles, scrolled, with dark sunk panels between them and a rosette over each, standing on a plain frieze: twelve across the main front south of the pavilion (x 447-852 px, about 35 px or 0.49 m apart), each about 32 px (0.45 m) high and 12 px (0.17 m) wide, their feet at y 432 px (8.5 m) and the corona's soffit at about y 400 px (9.0 m); the oblique (the right print) carries the same row round the south-west corner and along the south flank. Built as K10's scrolled console in the walls' stone (wall_head.blocks, T-3186, as 1901's), 0.45 m high and 0.17 m wide at no more than 0.5 m apart, their tops under the corona's soffit, standing on a frieze 0.32 m under the cornice's foot, the most the upper storey's lintels leave under it, so the consoles' feet stand at 8.39 m against the print's 8.5 m (the build's corona stands about 0.15 m under the print's, within tolerance); the projection (0.19 m) is the most the corona's soffit covers, and the carving is the kit's generic scroll. The rosettes over the consoles are not built.

roof_form.note: A slated mansard over the front with a gabled dormer, and the north pavilion's own steep hipped roof, on the square-on photograph (the left of the two views, Chicagology; 71.5 px/m on the front's plane, grade at y 1040 px).

front_bays.note: T-3562: the entrance's centre (s -0.7 m, in the block past the north corner, the 1908 Daily News picture (DN-0005529, the owner's 640 x 461 px copy; camera daily_news_dn0005529.json, 3.3 px rms)) and the two-storey window column at s 7.7 m (x 536 px on the square-on Chicagology print, from the front's north corner at x 100 px; 71.5 px/m on the front's plane), which the remodel kept over the new bay. chimneys.note: Two tall stacks on the square-on photograph (the left of the two views, Chicagology; 71.5 px/m on the front's plane, grade at y 1040 px): the north one over the stair projection behind the pavilion (x 85-130 px) (T-3562: read through the solved square-on camera its shaft, x 145-192 px at 29.8 m from the eye, centres about 0.33 m north of the north wall's line, over the stair projection, and its head is bare, a stone cap with no pot on it; it is built on the north wall's cornice, astride the wall line with its outer face at the cornice's 0.45 m edge (v -0.075), the furthest out K01 carries a stack on a house with no side parapet, about 0.25 m short of the print's, and it names its own pots as none) and the south one over the south flank near the front (x 785-820 px, also the oblique's broad stack). Their exact plans are reconstructed. T-3561: the south stack read off both prints and rebuilt. Triangulated through the two solved cameras (its south-west arris at x 830 px on the square-on and x 1765 px on the oblique), its west face stands about 1.6 m back from the front and its south face in line with the print's main south wall, which the oblique shows standing about 0.75 m inside the corner bay's south face (the open set-out in the match records): so it is the stack 'carried up from the flank wall past the mansard' of the oblique, standing on the south cornice. T-3562 built the set-out, so the south wall stands at v 9.72 and the stack on its cornice (on_cornice, v 9.65), its south face in line with the print's main south wall, its west face at u 15.86. Its plan, 1.26 m along the flank by 0.75 m: the square-on's 50 px west face at its depth (0.75 m), and along the flank the least that holds the four flues its head carries (below), four of K15's 0.21 m flues each with 0.1 m of stone between, 1.24 m, made a whole 12 half-bricks; its west face stays at u 15.86, so it grows 0.16 m toward the rear. It had been 1.1 m, the oblique's 60 px south face read through that view's camera, whose scale on this side of the house is not settled (its match record). Its head is read off both prints: the corbelled head's foot at about 13.6-13.8 m, the cap's top at about 14.3-14.5 m (top_m 14.45), a clay pot on each of three flues. T-3562 re-read the pots: on the oblique they stand 57-65 px over the cap's near edge (x 1730-1800, y 72-145 px), against the head's 43 px from the cap's top down to the corbels' foot (0.7 m), so about 0.95-1.05 m by the head's scale; and against the head in a render of the build, whose 1.0 m pots stand 1.14 times the head's height where the print's stand 1.4 times it, nearer 1.2 m: slender pots, three dark and fluted, about 0.15-0.18 m across. They take K15's long pot, 1.1 m over the cap (to 15.55 m), the middle of those readings, where the kit's tall one (0.72 m) stood about 0.3-0.5 m short. T-3562: and a fourth, the pale shape nearest the street (x 1737-1758 px): enlarged, it carries a rolled lip at its top (y 70-77 px) and stands from the cap to a top in line with the three dark pots' (their tops at y 82, 90 and 98 px, stepping down about 8-10 px a pot as the row recedes; this one's at 72 px, the next step nearer). It is pale where they are dark because it is the one pot seen whole: with the sun and the camera both to the south-west, the nearest pot shows its lit west side, and each pot behind it shows only the shaded sliver it leaves past the pot in front. So the head carries four pots in its row, each K15's long pot. The pots stand in a row back from the street, so the stack is turned (across 'x'), and it names its own four flues where the north stack keeps two. Both stacks are K15's stone stack, its courses overridden by the head the print draws (three corbel courses, a 0.15 m cap): the oblique's lit west face is as pale as the stone front and the square-on shows it coursed. T-3562: the sunk panels the oblique draws on its south face are built: three narrow ones side by side (x 1765-1825 px, three dark lines evenly across the shaded face), run from about 11.35 m (panel_foot_m: the stack stands on the flank's cornice, clear of the mansard, whose highest covering under it is 12.0 m) to 0.3 m under the corbelled head (13.45 m), each 0.15 m across and 0.05 m deep, cut in the stack's own stone (K15's stone panel). Their count and width are inferred from the lines' spacing on a small, half-shaded face; the north stack is bare in the square-on print and takes none (panelled: false).

rainwater.note: No downpipe is visible on the front; one on the north flank and one at the rear.

entrance_kit.note: T-3562: the remodelled entrance, read off the 1908 Daily News picture (DN-0005529, the owner's 640 x 461 px copy; camera daily_news_dn0005529.json, 3.3 px rms): a round-arched doorway at grade in the small stone block north of the front (v -1.33 to 0.0 m, its crown about 2.15 m over grade) under a square label, the opening reading black, an open vestibule arch. Built as K07's double door in a deep arch (k07.entrance.double_door_deep_arch): a 1.33 by 2.0 m opening one riser over grade, its voussoir ring 0.15 m under a keystone to 2.4 m, turned in the block's face (on_block_m, a K01 option this ticket added), no cheeks, no hood. The Chicagology prints' panelled door, its pedimented hood on two brackets and the stoop with its swept railed cheeks, newels and landing wing are Joseph Sears's front before the 1902 remodel (the owner's ruling, T-3562, 2026-11-21) and are not built for 1904. The front yard is the lot's: the street line at lot u 44.29 m, the front at 34.96 m.

bays.note: Read off the square-on photograph (the left of the two views, Chicagology; 71.5 px/m on the front's plane, grade at y 1040 px) against the 1911 sheet (s28fp-1815-b1): the pavilion across the front's north end, carried up an attic storey past the main cornice under its own steep hipped roof (T-3156: its paired lights x 200-325 px and y 390-250 px, its eave at y 210 px, 11.6 m; the main eave stopping square at its cheeks): the photograph's quoined pavilion runs x 100-390 px (4.0 m) with the door in its south half. T-3562: built so, re-read through the square-on camera (x 160-447 px there, s 0-4.0 m): its dentil band and quoins stop over the door's south half (the door's south jamb at s 4.13 m, the narrow light from s 4.01 m) and the oblique draws no cheek beside the door, so the pavilion is SHALLOW, 0.1 m proud (K08's least), 3.88 m wide from the north corner (flush_corner; 0.12 m short of the print's so the narrow light's lintel clears the junction), its window recesses run back through the wall (shallow), and the door is cut through its edge (cut_by_door, a K01 option T-3562 added: the face cut back from the door's north jamb past the cheek between sill and head). Its windows re-read: the principal storey's centred at s 1.40 m (x 228-295 px), the second storey's at 2.0 m (x 265-342 px) and the attic's paired lights at 2.0 m (x 240-362 px), widened to 1.7 m; the attic storey slated at its sides (K08's storey cheeks, 0.75 m each, as 1823's), leaving a 2.38 m stone front against the print's 2.37 m (x 217-387 px); the coursing carried up to the attic's foot (9.05 m). T-3562: the pavilion's own dentil band and the attic's stone shoulders read off the square-on print (71.5 px/m, grade at y 1040 px): the band a smooth course at y 437-452 px over a row of dentils to y 468 px (8.0-8.43 m, about 0.2 m over the second storey's window heads and 0.6 m under the main cornice's line), x 155-447 px across the pavilion, five or six dentils a segment at about 16-19 px; built as K08's corbel table carrying the attic storey (a 0.21 m course 0.15 m proud on 0.1 m blocks at 0.22 m, down to 0.43 m under the line), the attic's foot brought down to 8.43 m with it (its lights' sill raised to keep them at 9.25 m) and the coursing carried up the whole pavilion, as the print courses its attic; beside the attic each cheek is the pavilion's stone up to a capped block, its cap at y 280-295 px (to 10.63 m) and a second band at y 325-337 px (to 10.0 m), both overhanging the pavilion's edges, the slate rising from the cap (K08's cheek shoulder, a T-3562 option: 2.2 m of stone, 0.2 m caps 0.12 m proud, the second at 1.57 m), the slate cheeks then 0.05 m proud of the coursing. T-3562: the cheeks RAKED (K08 cheeks.raked, a T-3562 option), as the square-on print draws them: over each shoulder the attic's wall stops, and the slate slopes from the stone front's edge under the end of the crown's cornice (11.45 m) down to the cheek's outer edge on the cap (10.63 m; the print's slope from about y 230 to y 282 px, 0.6-0.75 m out, about 50 degrees), run back 5.0 m, the crown's depth (inferred: the print shows only its street end; a hipped crown's sides carried down past its cornice to the shoulders is the reading that leaves the print's sky over the north cheek), the pavilion's own eaves and flat top giving way to the crown's (mansard's note); on the north flank the sheet's stair projection 0.86 m behind the front, 1.55 m out on the sheet and built 1.2 m out, K08's deepest pavilion (its face in shadow at x 45-100 px), and on the south flank the sheet's canted bay 9-13 m behind the front (lot u 18.1-25.6), its storeys reconstructed. T-3562 (the owner's ruling, 2026-11-21: 1904 is the remodelled front): the 1908 Daily News picture (DN-0005529, the owner's 640 x 461 px copy; camera daily_news_dn0005529.json, 3.3 px rms) shows the ground floor Arthur Heun's 1902 remodel gave the house, the sheet's own reading: the corner bay with its pierced balcony is gone and a one-storey stone bay stands across the front's middle (front_bay: x 205-290 px, v 1.24-7.04 m, its face 1.2 m proud), three tall transomed lights in its front (2.05-4.17 m over grade) and a narrow one in its south cheek, two barred basement lights under the outer ones, an iron railing on a stone ledge across its front at its basement's head (about 1.46 m; K08's floor balcony, squared with an iron rail, options this ticket added) and a row of modillions under a moulded crown and a plain blocking course to about 5.7 m (K08's corbel table under a plain stone storey, the carving under the bar on this print); and north of the north corner a small one-storey stone block carrying the arched entrance at grade (north_entry: v -1.95 to 0.46 m, 0.2 m before the front, capped about 3.06 m under a moulded cornice; set out past the corner, set_out_m, and run 0.96 m back along the flank to the stair projection, set_out_back_m, K01 and K08 options this ticket added). The pavilion no longer has the old door cut through its edge. The block's depth along the flank, its cap's moulding and the bay's flat top are reconstructed (L-k01-1815-sears-1893).

mansard.note: The slated mansard's curb under its cresting at y 150 px (12.4 m) on the square-on photograph (the left of the two views, Chicagology; 71.5 px/m on the front's plane, grade at y 1040 px), 2.9 m over the wall head; the gabled dormer centred at x 535 px, its sash x 498-580 px and y 345-230 px; a gabled dormer on the south flank in the oblique. The pavilion's steep roof (apex y 75 px, 13.5 m) is K01's hipped crown over it, raised by T-3156 onto the attic storey's wall head: its eave at y 210 px (11.6 m, 2.35 m over the main eave), the crown's eave 0.5 m past the attic's face (the print's x 165-360 px), its faces at 52 degrees so the apex stands about 13.8 m (the print's apex 13.5 m, read in front of the ridge's set-back). T-3562: the south flank's dormer read off the oblique, where it stands just east of the tall south stack (the stack's shaft x 1740-1820 px, the dormer's gable x 1820-1880 px): its centre about 1.4 m behind the stack's (the stack's 1.1 m shaft spans 80 px there), at 13.9 m from the rear, its body clear of the stack (it stood at 9.0 m, read off no picture, and so out of the oblique's frame); T-3562 then took it to 13.83 m, 1.4 m behind the stack's centre still, when the stack was widened toward the rear for its fourth flue (the chimneys' note), so its body stays clear of the stack. T-3562: the curb's iron cresting, the pavilion's cross and the street dormer re-read off the square-on print (66.7 px/m on the mansard's face): along the curb a pierced iron band, its top rail a dark line at y 146-150 px with hung ornaments under it and its foot on a dark line at y 178 over the slates, about 0.45 m, the sky showing over its rail and no deck behind it; built as the K10 kit's iron cresting 0.45 m high on the street curb and the south flank's (K01's north side; the oblique shows the curb under its cresting there), stopped short either side of the pavilion's crown where the crown stands through the curb (k01_mansard_deck.crown_gap); its pattern, hung trefoils in the print, is the kit's.
